Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

# Report: linkvault domain and architecture patterns (Web Researcher 2)

I checked the Python behaviours below by running them locally. The sandbox runs Python 3.9.6, while the contract targets 3.11 or later. The sources for items 1, 2, 4 and 5 are the RFCs and docs.python.org pages, plus my own knowledge of them, because I only fetched part of RFC 9110. I fetched RFC 9110 §8.6 and §11.1 and RFC 6585 §4. The other RFC 9110 sections are cited from memory, and the section numbers match the document's table of contents.

## Key findings

**1. HTTP semantics**

1. **The contract's 204 rule conflicts with RFC 9110.**
   - RFC 9110 §8.6 says a server MUST NOT send `Content-Length` in any 1xx or 204 response. I confirmed this in the fetched text.
   - The contract (Conventions, E6) says a 204 MUST send `Content-Length: 0`.
   - Python's `http.client` and `urllib` accept a 204 with `Content-Length: 0`. I tested it and got `status 204, body b''`. So the contract rule is safe to implement, but it is a deliberate deviation. The spec should say so, so nobody "fixes" it.
2. **302 (§15.4.3) is fine as written.** `Location` plus `Content-Length: 0` and an empty body is valid. The 302 response is not cacheable by default.
3. **429 and `Retry-After`.**
   - RFC 6585 §4 says 429 responses MUST NOT be stored by a cache. A body is optional and `Retry-After` is a MAY.
   - RFC 9110 §10.2.3 allows `Retry-After` as either delta-seconds (a non-negative decimal integer) or an HTTP-date. The contract's `window_start + 60 - now` always falls in 1 to 60, so it is valid delta-seconds.
4. **410 (§15.5.11) and 413 (§15.5.14).**
   - 410 Gone is appropriate for the expired link.
   - A server MAY close the connection on 413 so the unread request body cannot be mis-parsed as the next request. That justifies the contract's `Connection: close`.
5. **urllib follows redirects by default.**
   - `urllib.request.urlopen('/r')` on a 302 silently returned the target's body, so tests must not use urllib for E7.
   - `http.client.HTTPConnection.request` and `getresponse` return the raw 302, with `Location` readable through `getheader`.
6. **urllib error behaviour, as tested.**
   - A 4xx or 5xx raises `HTTPError`. It carries `.code`, `.headers['Retry-After']` and `.read()` with the body.
   - Connection refused raises `URLError`, where `e.reason` is a `ConnectionRefusedError`.
   - An unresolvable host raises `URLError` with a gaierror reason.
   - Several client failures are not `URLError`. A malformed server URL like `http://[::1` raises a plain `ValueError`, and a URL without a scheme (`nohost`) raises `ValueError: unknown url type`. A port above 65535 (such as `http://127.0.0.1:99999/`) was not tested separately in `urllib`; it falls under the `ValueError` in finding 12 in the usual case.
   - A timeout raised `URLError` here (the `ConnectionRefusedError` case came out as a `URLError` as well). On some Python versions a socket timeout can surface as `TimeoutError` or `socket.timeout` directly.
   - The client's exit-3 handler needs to catch `URLError`, `OSError`, `http.client.HTTPException` and `TimeoutError`.
   - Malformed `--server` values should map to exit 2 (usage) via `ValueError`, not exit 3. The contract does not say which, so the spec should.
7. **Default `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` behaviour breaks the contract if not overridden.**
   - Methods without a `do_X` method, such as PUT, PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS, get 501 with an HTML body. The contract requires 404 `not_found` JSON for every unlisted (method, path) pair, so the handler must define all of them. HEAD on a valid path also needs a decision.
   - `send_error` and `log_message` write HTML and stderr output respectively. Override both. Nothing may reach stdout.
   - `protocol_version` defaults to HTTP/1.0, so the connection closes after each response. That is fine and simplest; keep-alive needs correct framing everywhere.
   - `Content-Length` header values need defensive parsing: non-numeric, negative or duplicated values. The contract does not say what status these get. I suggest 400 `invalid_request`. This ordering question should be settled in the spec.

**2. Fixed-window rate limiting**

8. **Structure.** A dict keyed by `token_hash` holds `(window_start, count)`, guarded by one `threading.Lock`. The check-and-increment must happen inside one critical section.
9. **Pruning.** Resetting the entry when `window_start` changes already bounds memory to one entry per token. No separate pruning is needed. Counters are keyed by the hash of a valid token only, so unknown tokens cannot grow the dict, because auth (401) comes before the rate limit.
10. **`Retry-After`** is `window_start + 60 - now`. It is never 0, since `now % 60 < 60`. With the fake clock at window start plus 10, it is 50, which matches AC9.
11. **Pitfalls that follow from the contract.**
    - Count only after auth succeeds, and count before the 413/400/404/409 checks. The contract counts every request that reaches the rate-limit step, whatever its final status.
    - Read "now" once per request and use that one value for both the window and `Retry-After`.
    - A 429 request still increments the counter, which is harmless.
    - The route step must run first, so an unknown path or an invalid slug on E5/E6 never counts.
    - E7 redirects, E1 and admin routes are exempt.
    - Moving the fake clock to a new window resets the effective count, because the stored `window_start` no longer matches.

**3. Auth**

12. **Scheme case.** RFC 9110 §11.1 says the scheme is a case-insensitive token, and RFC 6750 §2.1 is the Bearer syntax. The contract says "strict" `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A strict implementation is allowed: it splits on a single space, and the scheme match is case-sensitive or case-insensitive depending on the decision.
    - The spec must pick one. I recommend accepting the scheme case-insensitively, since that is RFC-correct, with exactly one space. Anything malformed returns 401, and the token should be exact and non-empty.
    - A test that sends `bearer` lowercase and expects 401 would conflict with that choice. The contract's wording "malformed" is ambiguous, so state the decision explicitly.
13. **Token storage.**
    - Store `hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()` and look up by that hash. A lookup by hash through the DB index is not a meaningful timing leak, because the attacker does not control the hash input to the comparison.
    - Before hashing, check the token format against `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. Non-ASCII bytes in a header would otherwise cause problems. The header arrives as latin-1-decoded text, so `.encode()` could produce odd bytes. Reject on regex mismatch first, which means 401.
14. **Admin key comparison.**
    - `hmac.compare_digest(str, str)` raises `TypeError` if either string has non-ASCII characters. I confirmed this: "comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported". That would surface as a 500.
    - Compare bytes: `hmac.compare_digest(supplied.encode('utf-8','surrogateescape'), key.encode('utf-8','surrogateescape'))`. Bytes comparison with a non-ASCII key returned True when I tested it.
    - Header values arrive as latin-1-decoded text, so the safest approach is to re-encode the supplied header with latin-1 and encode the CLI key with UTF-8. A CLI `--admin-key` containing non-ASCII characters then only matches if the client sends the same bytes.
    - The spec should say which encoding it uses. An alternative is to compare SHA-256 digests of both sides, which sidesteps encoding errors but still needs a clear rule. A missing header must yield 401, not an exception.
    - The server should hold the admin key as bytes, and a CLI `--admin-key ''` is rejected with exit 2.

**4. `urlsplit` pitfalls (tested)**

15. **Results table.**

    | Input | Result |
    |---|---|
    | `http://` | scheme `http`, hostname `None` |
    | `http:///path` | hostname `None` |
    | `http://user@/x` | hostname `None` |
    | `http:example.com` | hostname `None` |
    | `http://:80/` | hostname `None`, port 80 |
    | `javascript:alert(1)` | scheme `javascript`, hostname `None` |
    | `HTTP://Example.COM/A` | scheme `http`, hostname lowercased |
    | `http://[::1` | `urlsplit` raises `ValueError('Invalid IPv6 URL')` |
    | `http://[::1]:99999/x` | hostname `::1`, `.port` raises `ValueError` |
    | `http://h:abc/` | hostname `h`, `.port` raises `ValueError` |
    | `http://h:/` | hostname `h`, port `None` |

16. **urlsplit strips characters silently.** `urlsplit('http://a\tb.com/')` gave hostname `ab.com`, and `http://exa\nmple.com` gave `example.com`. Python strips tab, CR and LF before parsing (a security fix in recent 3.x releases). So the whitespace and control-character check MUST run on the raw string before `urlsplit`, or such URLs would slip through.
    - `http://a b/` has hostname `a b`. It is rejected only by the explicit whitespace check.
17. **Recommended validation order.**
    1. Type is `str`.
    2. Length is at most 2048. Count code points, i.e. `len(url)`.
    3. No code point below 0x21 and no 0x7F. The contract's wording "< 0x21 or 0x7F" covers all whitespace except Unicode spaces such as U+00A0 and U+2028.
    4. `try: s = urlsplit(url) except ValueError` gives 400.
    5. `s.scheme in ('http','https')`. `urlsplit` already lowercases the scheme, so no extra case handling is needed.
    6. `s.hostname` is truthy.
    - Never touch `.port` unless the spec says to. If it does not, `http://h:abc/` is accepted. The contract only requires a non-empty hostname, so that is contract-conformant, but it is worth stating.
    - Non-ASCII hostnames (`http://é.com/`) also pass. State that this is accepted.
    - Whether the 2048 limit counts code points or UTF-8 bytes is another ambiguity; the contract says "characters", so code points.

**5. Testing patterns**

18. **Server subprocess.**
    - Start with `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-m','linkvault','serve','--db',db,'--admin-key',k,'--port','0'], stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, text=True, cwd=ROOT)`.
    - Read exactly one line from stdout with a timeout, because `readline()` blocks forever if the server crashes. A reader thread or a poll on the process is the common pattern. The line must match `^LISTENING http://127\.0\.0\.1:(\d+)\r?\n$`.
    - Do not let stderr fill the pipe. Either drain it in a thread or write it to a temp file.
19. **Shutdown test.**
    - On POSIX: `proc.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)`, then `proc.wait(timeout=5)`, and assert `returncode == 0`. Repeat with SIGTERM.
    - On Windows: create the process with `creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, then call `proc.send_signal(signal.CTRL_BREAK_EVENT)`.
    - The server must install handlers for `signal.SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, and `SIGBREAK` where it exists (`hasattr(signal,'SIGBREAK')`). `SIGTERM` handling on Windows is not reliable.
20. **A deadlock pitfall in the server's shutdown design.**
    - `server.shutdown()` called from a signal handler on the same thread that runs `serve_forever()` deadlocks.
    - Use one of two patterns. Run `serve_forever()` in a worker thread and have the main thread wait on a `threading.Event` that the signal handler sets. Or have the handler start a thread that calls `shutdown()`.
    - After shutdown, call `server_close()`, then close the DB, then `sys.exit(0)`.
    - Set `daemon_threads = True` on `ThreadingHTTPServer` (it already is). Otherwise `server_close()` joins non-daemon handler threads via `block_on_close` and can exceed the 5 s budget.
21. **SQLite and threads.** Handler threads share one connection only if `check_same_thread=False` and a lock serialises all use, or each thread opens its own connection. R14 depends on this.
    - The atomic click is `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`. Under multiple connections, set a busy timeout (for example `timeout=30`). WAL mode helps, but the contract does not ask for it.
    - The simplest option is one connection plus one lock, with the expiry check and the click done in the same critical section.
22. **Non-redirect-following test requests.** Use `http.client.HTTPConnection('127.0.0.1', port, timeout=10)`, then `request(method, path, body, headers)` and `getresponse()`. Read the body before reusing the connection. Never use `urllib` for E7.
    - For the 413 test, send a `Content-Length` of 8193 with no body. The server must reply without reading it. A test that does send 8193 bytes can see a connection reset.
    - A malformed bearer header test can use `http.client` and bypass any client-side normalisation.
23. **Concurrency test (AC11).**
    - Use `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=50)`, and give each worker its own `HTTPConnection`, since a connection is not thread-safe. Use a `threading.Barrier(50)` to line the requests up.
    - Assert all responses are 302, then assert `clicks == 50` through E5. Make sure the server's listen backlog can cope: `socketserver.TCPServer.request_queue_size` defaults to 5, so raise it (for example to 128) or a burst of 50 simultaneous connects can see resets on some platforms.
24. **Fake-clock tests.** Frozen time makes AC7 and AC9 deterministic. Start with `--fake-clock 2026-01-01T00:00:10Z` (a window start plus 10 s), and move the clock via E8.

## Constraints the spec MUST respect

- Nothing but the `LISTENING` line goes to stdout, from the server or from library code. Override `log_message` to write to stderr, and never use `print` for logs. Flush after the ready line. Print it only after the socket is bound and the DB is open.
- Check the whitespace and control characters on the raw URL before `urlsplit`. Wrap `urlsplit` in `except ValueError`.
- Never call `hmac.compare_digest` on non-ASCII `str` values. Compare bytes.
- Define handlers for every HTTP method the server might see, or the default 501 HTML response breaks the "unlisted pair returns 404 `not_found`" rule. Override `send_error` to produce JSON.
- Keep the precedence order: route 404, auth 401, rate limit 429, size 413, JSON 400, validation 400, state. An invalid slug on E5/E6/E7 is 404 at the route step, before auth and before any rate counting.
- E7 is not rate-limited and not authenticated. `GET /healthz` is also exempt.
- The fake clock route exists only with `--fake-clock`. Otherwise POST `/v1/admin/clock` returns 404, and it must not reach auth.
- A 204 and a 302 must both send `Content-Length: 0`. The 204 case deviates from RFC 9110 §8.6 by design.
- Tests use `http.client`, never `urllib`, for E7.
- Use `ThreadingHTTPServer` with `daemon_threads = True`, a signal-safe shutdown that does not call `shutdown()` from the serving thread, and a clean exit code 0.
- Bind exactly 127.0.0.1 (not `localhost`, not `0.0.0.0`).
- Exit code 3 is for a bind failure or DB open failure. Exit code 2 is for argparse errors. argparse errors for an invalid `--port` or `--rate-limit` need type functions that raise `argparse.ArgumentTypeError`. A DB parent directory that does not exist must exit 3.
